transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-28
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Meridian Procurement), David Ortiz (Meridian CISO), Samir Patel (Meridian Finance)

Summary:
Quick procurement/governance alignment focused on MSA/DPA exceptions, SLA and billing model for a pilot -> production transition. Customer raised narrow DPA exception questions, asked for committed pricing model and evidence of SOC/attestations and KMS options.

Topics discussed:
- MSA redlines and specific commercial terms to expedite onboarding
- DPA exception scope (PII vs telemetry) and controls (KMS, audit logs)
- SLA numbers and remedies (latency P95/P99, availability)
- Billing model for reserved capacity and overage treatment
- Security artifacts and evidence required by Meridian

Action items (as discussed in call): see metadata list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick agenda — we want to align on the MSA redlines, the DPA exception you flagged, and then the billing model for the pilot to prod path. Priya's with me to run numbers.
[00:28] Laura: Yeah thanks. We have some strict timelines, uh, procurement wants vendor gating closed by mid-March if possible. Our legal team already flagged three DPA clauses they want scoped as exceptions.
[00:45] David: Right and from security we need clarity on where keys live, so KMS or customer-managed? also audit logs retention and role-based access.
[01:10] Priya: Understood. On KMS we support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer KMS via BYOK integrations. There can be differences in telemetry — if you choose customer KMS you lose some server-side tokenization but you keep full key control.
[01:36] Samir: And that has billing implications? Does customer KMS add fees? we need to understand any additional costs.
[01:48] Alex: Good question. For BYOK there may be a small per-key management fee in some on-prem/private deployments, but for hosted we can often absorb it — we'll call that out in the pricing appendix.
[02:10] Laura: The DPA exceptions they're asking for are mostly around storing certain customer identifiers for up to 30 days for troubleshooting. we want to know if Redwood can carve that out and apply additional controls, like encryption at rest with HSM and limited access logs.
[02:36] Priya: You can do both. We can annotate the data categories in the DPA and apply a tighter access control and audit log retention. The tradeoff is operational complexity during incident response.
[03:00] David: Another thing, we require SOC 2 type II evidence and the contract needs an indemnity carve-out for regulated-data breaches.
[03:15] Alex: We have SOC 2 reports — I'll share the latest. For indemnity, we typically follow our commercial terms but we can look at narrowing the exposure. we'll flag the legal team to propose text.
[03:35] Laura: Also, on SLA — are you offering P95/P99 latency commitments for the dedicated pool? We need predictable P99 for user-facing flows.
[03:49] Priya: For dedicated capacity we commit to availability SLAs and provide performance profiles. Typical P95 numbers depend on model and sequence length; P99 is more variable but we run a reserved capacity sizing exercise — I'll produce estimated P99 at projected Q3 QPS.
[04:12] Samir: ok we need that estimate to sign off from finance. Also need an example of overage billing calculation — is it blended unit price or different tiers?
[04:28] Alex: We usually offer committed units at a reduced rate and overage at on-demand pricing; we can create a blended examples sheet for your volumes.
[04:40] Laura: Great. On DPA exceptions, one of the asks was for data residency — can Redwood promise EU-only storage for certain tenants?
[04:55] Priya: Yes for Private deployments or VPCs we can pin region. For hosted, region pinning is possible with data residency add-ons, but it depends on model hosting region availability.
[05:18] David: For the audit, we'd also like to see request-level logs — who called what model and what route. Is that available?
[05:28] Alex: We provide request logs and we can surface them in the console; retention can be configured. there are cost/tradeoffs with long retention.
[05:42] Laura: Any third-party subprocessors where data could be exported? we need a list for procurement.
[05:51] Priya: We use common cloud infra providers for hosted — we will provide subprocessors list and scopes. For private deployments there are none beyond your infra.
[06:05] Samir: About pricing approvals — our procurement needs an approved price list and also a sign-off path for renewals after pilot. Is that something Redwood covers?
[06:18] Alex: We'll provide an initial term quote and a renewal anchor; finance can propose the renewal formula. we'll document it in the pricing appendix.
[06:32] Laura: One of our concerns is vendor lock-in and model variant fallbacks — can we require hints in the contract about fallback to open quantized models if Redwood hosted model is deprecated?
[06:46] Priya: We can include a model deprecation/fallback policy in the SLA appendices; we do version pinning and compatible model fallback rules.
[07:02] David: Security question: do you support customer-managed identity integration — SSO/SAML and RBAC?
[07:10] Alex: Yes, SAML/SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC are supported. we'll attach the integration guide.
[07:22] Laura: Good, also can you outline the escalation path — who does Meridian call at 2am for an incident?
[07:29] Alex: We'll provide an on-call escalation matrix for the dedicated tier, including phone pager if you buy the premium SLA.
[07:40] Samir: For billing, can you produce a sample invoice showing committed vs overage lines? procurement wants to understand cashflow.
[07:50] Priya: We'll include a sample invoice and show amortization of committed credits across months.
[08:05] Laura: On DPA exceptions — legal asked that certain data categories be redlined. can Redwood accept scoped exceptions limited to debugging logs for only triage?
[08:18] Alex: We can take that as a limited exception with additional controls — encryption, access logging, restricted retention, and a covenant to purge. We'll propose language.
[08:31] David: There's also an export control clause; are there scenarios where model output or logs could be accessible outside region due to vendor tools?
[08:42] Priya: For hosted, some tooling may use third-party analytics; we can limit that and mark it in subprocessors. For private, it's fully customer-controlled.
[08:55] Laura: Ok, so immediate asks: redlined MSA, DPA exception scope, SOC report, sample invoice, and committed-pricing spreadsheet.
[09:06] Alex: Exactly. We'll commit to those deliverables and timeline.
[09:14] Samir: one more — do you have a stop-gap SLA for the pilot? we might need a short-term SLA with credits.
[09:23] Priya: We can propose a pilot SLA with scaled credits — less than enterprise but better than pure on-demand.
[09:33] Laura: On timelines — procurement wants gating complete by March 17. is that feasible?
[09:40] Alex: With your cooperation on the DPA scope and a quick legal review, yes. we'll aim to deliver the redlined MSA by Mar 3 and the pricing model by Mar 5, so internal reviews can happen.
[09:56] David: We'll schedule the security deep-dive after we see the SOC report and the proposed DPA text.
[10:04] Alex: Great. Anything else?
[10:08] Laura: Not from procurement; will follow up with a list of in-scope data types.
[10:12] Samir: Finance will review the sample invoice and confirm cadence.
[10:16] Priya: I'll run the performance numbers and include P95/P99 estimates and assumptions.
[10:24] Alex: Perfect. Recap — we'll send: redlined MSA, SOC attestation, pricing appendix, committed-volume model, sample invoice, subprocessors list, and schedule the security deep-dive.
[10:38] Laura: thanks all.
[10:40] David: thanks.
[10:41] Samir: thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Alex to share updated MSA with tracked changes and pricing appendix by 2027-03-03.
- Priya to run committed-volume billing model and P99/P95 performance estimates (due 2027-03-05).
- David to share security attestation requirements and lock down DPA exception items (due 2027-03-07).
- Samir to confirm finance sign-off criteria and preferred billing cadence (due 2027-03-09).
